R061-01.notes: B: counting during closing week; narrator reads back-page list of unreturned loans (a record of lending on trust). A: no persuasion, store closes. C: trumpet is a cheap student model with stuck valves, and Arno crosses it off; no sale mentioned. D: no argument; narrator only asks why it matters.

R061-02.notes: 'He only wanted to know what had been there' and 'I'll read it' when narrator says nobody will read the ledger. A: 'Not to sell it'; dealer takes stock. B: cases go to new owners, no list required. C: no teaching motive stated.

R061-03.notes: 'Instead he opened the ledger...drew a neat stroke' contrasts with the expected laugh/dismissal. B: no evidence of rudeness. C: narrator calls it cheap. D: expectation says nothing about the man's delay.

R061-04.notes: Drawing a stroke through a ledger line = a line. A, B, D are other senses of 'stroke' that don't fit writing in a ledger.

R061-05.notes: Stated directly: 'to play in his high school's spring concert.' A, C unsupported; B misuses 'dented' (the borrowed trumpet itself is dented). Minor timeline note, not flagged: a man in high school in 1987 who is 'only a few years younger than Arno' implies Arno was very young when running the shop then, which strains a little but is possible.

R061-06.notes: List is of 'things that had gone out the door and not come back'; only one crossed out means the rest never returned. A: contradicts Arno's meticulousness. C: trumpet is cheap. D: some entries thirty years old.

R061-07.notes: Generous phrasing ('mean to') credits borrowers' intentions despite unreturned items. A: no anger; tone is calm. B: no plan to demand anything; store is closing. D: no regret expressed.

R061-08.notes: 'my uncle Arno' plus first person 'I' who helps count = relative. B: Arno is referred to in third person. C: the man is described from outside. D: first-person, limited to narrator's perceptions ('I expected').

R061-09.notes: Keeping ledger under his own arm, not letting narrator carry it = personal attachment. A: overreads; narrator was trusted on the ladder all week. B: dealer takes stock, not the ledger; Arno keeps it. C: no relief indicated.

R061-10.notes: After 'the man left, and Arno went back to the numbers,' narrator 'climbed down from the ladder and looked at the back page.' A: no reading that early; she hadn't seen the line written. C: trap; narrator climbed down first. D: list read on fourth afternoon, not the last day.
